 Follow Fans Vote 'The Dark Knight' as the Best Film of the Last 25 Years
 DeAnna Janes Thu, October 22, 2026 at 3:10 AM UTC 3 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Fans Vote 'The Dark Knight' as the Best Film of the Last 25 Years The fans have spoken, and The Dark Knight has officially been crowned the fan-voted greatest film of the last 25 years by Rotten Tomatoes .
 The landmark superhero thriller directed by Christopher Nolan transforms the classic comic-book story into a gritty crime saga, becoming an era-defining film and a gold standard for superhero movies. The film tops the publication's fan-selected list, which celebrates movies released during the site's first 25 years.

 Released in July 2008 , the action epic stars Christian Bale as Batman, alongside Aaron Eckhart as Harvey Dent, Michael Caine as Alfred, Morgan Freeman as Lucius Fox, Maggie Gyllenhaal as Rachel Dawes, and Gary Oldman as Commissioner Gordon. Perhaps the most notable cast member, however, is the late Heath Ledger , whose portrayal of the Joker is widely considered one of the most memorable performances in superhero-movie history.
 Heath Ledger's Joker Became a Defining Movie Performance 
 To prepare for the role, Ledger reportedly isolated himself in a London hotel room for about a month, experimenting with voices and keeping a journal to develop the Joker's disturbing personality.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In a 2007 interview with The New York Times , Ledger described the character as a "psychopathic, mass-murdering, schizophrenic clown with zero empathy."
 He also discussed the toll of immersing himself in the role, saying, "Last week I probably slept an average of two hours a night. I couldn't stop thinking. My body was exhausted, and my mind was still going."
 Ledger died in January 2008 , months before the film premiered. His performance was subsequently recognized with a posthumous Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor at the 2009 Oscars, making the role an especially poignant part of his legacy.
 Why 'The Dark Knight' Still Stands Out 
 Nolan's film distinguished itself by treating Gotham City as a crime-ridden metropolis rather than a fantastical comic-book setting. Batman's battle against the Joker becomes a psychological struggle over fear, morality, and how far people will go when society's rules begin to crumble.
 Advertisement Advertisement The film's Rotten Tomatoes critics' consensus praises its ambition, describing it as "dark, complex, and unforgettable," and calling it "a richly thrilling crime saga." That blend of blockbuster action and character-driven storytelling helped the movie reach audiences beyond traditional superhero fans.
 Its influence can still be felt across the genre, with filmmakers continuing to explore darker, more grounded takes on comic-book characters. The film also remains a standout in Nolan's career, helping establish the director as one of Hollywood's most influential blockbuster filmmakers.
 Fans Put the Batman Classic Ahead of the Competition
 The Dark Knight took the top spot in Rotten Tomatoes ' fan-voted ranking, ahead of other acclaimed films including Interstellar and The Matrix . The list spans superhero adventures, science-fiction epics, fantasy franchises, and award-winning dramas, reflecting the breadth of movies that have shaped popular culture over the past quarter century.
 The film also holds an impressive critical reputation: Rotten Tomatoes currently lists its Tomatometer score at 94%, though scores can change as ratings are updated.
 Advertisement Advertisement Nearly two decades after its release, The Dark Knight continues to resonate with moviegoers. Its combination of Nolan's ambitious direction, a gripping crime-thriller story, and Ledger's unforgettable Joker helps explain why fans have now placed it at the top of the last 25 years of cinema.
